verdict: Bank of America started 2026 strongly: revenue rose 7% to $30.3B, net interest income grew 9%, and net income rose 17% to $8.6B as every major business contributed.

segments.name: Net interest income
segments.note: The spread between what the bank earns on loans and investments and what it pays on deposits — its biggest single money source.

segments.name: Noninterest income
segments.note: Fees and markets income: asset management fees, investment banking fees and sales & trading revenue of $6.4B.

flow.costPlain: Money set aside for loans expected to go bad — the closest thing a bank has to a cost of goods sold.

opex.name: Compensation and benefits
opex.note: Pay and benefits for the bank's roughly 213,000 employees — well over half of all running costs.

opex.name: Information processing and communications
opex.note: Technology, data processing and communications — the plumbing of a digital bank.

opex.name: Occupancy and equipment
opex.note: Branches, offices, ATMs and the equipment in them.

opex.name: Product delivery and transaction related
opex.note: The cost of moving money: processing payments, producing cards and handling transactions.

opex.name: Marketing
opex.note: Advertising and promoting the bank's products.

opex.name: Other general operating
opex.note: Everything else that does not fit the lines above.

takeaways.title: Interest income did the heavy lifting
takeaways.text: Net interest income rose 9% to $15.7B — the spread between what the bank earns on loans and pays on deposits — as loan and deposit balances grew.

takeaways.title: Profit grew faster than revenue
takeaways.text: Net income rose 17% to $8.6B on 7% revenue growth: expenses rose more slowly than revenue (2.9 points of operating leverage), and credit costs stayed contained at $1.3B.

takeaways.title: EPS jumped 25%
takeaways.text: Diluted EPS rose 25% to $1.11 — faster than net income — because buybacks keep shrinking the share count: average diluted shares were down about 5% from a year ago.

oneTimers: Preferred stock dividends of $429M sit between net income ($8,584M) and the $8,155M applicable to common shareholders.
